summary: Validated all five acceptance criteria for server-side paid-duel region eligibility against a locally built and started production server (pnpm build && pnpm start), spoofing Vercel's edge geo headers via curl. AC-1 and AC-2 (/duel first-paint correctness for blocked and allowed regions, no flash) were verified by live request: the raw HTML response (before any JS execution) already contains the correct region copy/badges, and the embedded RSC payload carries the true server-resolved initialGeoAllowed value, not an optimistic default. AC-4 (/api/geo/ranked JSON shape) and AC-5 (money-movement enforcement untouched) were verified by my own independent live spot-checks on top of the upstream agents' diff-based confirmations. AC-3 (/duel/chips stake picker never visible to a blocked user) was verified with an explicit split: the anonymous-curl case was run live and, as the reviewer predicted, always shows the SignInGate regardless of region (auth gate precedes geo gate) — I did not treat that as passing or failing AC-3, since it would be a false signal either way. The load-bearing property (stake picker requires user && geoAllowed) was instead verified by direct code inspection of ChipDuelLobby.tsx's single ternary render chain, which has no other path to the money-moving markup. No live authenticated session was available in this environment to additionally confirm AC-3 by request. All five ACs PASS. Also walked the rendered UX (not just boolean logic) for all four kill-switch combinations; found one non-blocking, pre-existing UX nit (kill-switch-off is mislabeled as 'region restricted' rather than a neutral 'temporarily unavailable' message) which is the reviewer's already-filed warning finding, reconfirmed live by me on the (PAID_DUELS_ENABLED=false, NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED=true) combination — not a regression introduced by this diff and does not fail any AC. Cleaned up: killed both local servers, reverted the app/next-env.d.ts churn from my own pnpm build, working tree contains only the same files as the prior stages (no new production-code changes from me).
goal: Acceptance-validate: server-side paid-duel region eligibility renders the true region decision on /duel and /duel/chips on first paint (no flash), a shared edge-compatible headers-based helper is used, fail-closed posture is preserved, /api/geo/ranked's response shape is unchanged, and money-movement enforcement is unaffected.

exitCriteria.AC-3_chips_stake_picker_never_visible_wh: pass — verified by code inspection (auth-gated case) + live request (anonymous case, used to confirm the documented caveat, not as evidence of the property itself)
exitCriteria.AC-4_api_geo_ranked_shape_unchanged: pass — verified live (own independent check) + upstream diff confirmation
exitCriteria.AC-5_money_movement_enforcement_unregres: pass — verified by one independent live spot-check (401 on unauthenticated chip match POST) + upstream diff/grep confirmation

acResults.evidence: curl -H 'x-vercel-ip-country: US' -H 'x-vercel-ip-country-region: NY' http://localhost:3900/duel -> raw HTML body contains 'Not available in your region.' x2 and badge text 'unavailable' x2, as genuine markup (not a serialized JSON blob — confirmed by surrounding tags). Embedded RSC payload carries "initialGeoAllowed":false. Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate.

Same request with region CA -> raw HTML shows 'ranked' badge and 'Stake chips — winner takes all. Non-cashable.' subtitle for Chip Duels, 'coming soon' (not 'unavailable') for Tournaments, no blocked copy anywhere in the response. Same non-cacheable Cache-Control.

acResults.method: code inspection (load-bearing property) + live request (confirms the documented anonymous-SSR caveat, used only to avoid a false-pass, not as the AC-3 evidence itself)
acResults.evidence: Live: anonymous curl to /duel/chips for both NY and CA returns only the SignInGate ('Sign in...') — confirms ChipDuelLobby gates !user before !geoAllowed, exactly as the reviewer flagged, so an anonymous-curl assertion cannot observe the geo branch at all. Code: app/src/components/Duel/ChipDuelLobby.tsx:111-125 is a single ternary — !user ? SignInGate : !geoAllowed ? RegionRestricted : <stake picker + Find match> — with no other render path to the money-moving markup, and geoAllowed is sourced from useRankedEligibility(true, initialGeoAllowed) whose state is a non-nullable boolean seeded from the server and only ever overwritten by another server-derived boolean. No authenticated session was available in this environment to additionally confirm this live.

acResults.method: live request (own independent check) + citing upstream diff confirmation
acResults.evidence: GET /api/geo/ranked with NY headers -> {"allowed":false,"reason":"not_allowlisted"}; with CA headers -> {"allowed":true,"reason":null}. Shape matches the documented pre-existing contract. Verifier and reviewer independently diffed the route source against HEAD and found it byte-identical in shape construction.

acResults.method: own independent live spot-check + citing upstream diff/grep confirmation
acResults.evidence: git diff --name-only HEAD (re-run myself) touches none of paidDuelGuards.ts, chips/match/route.ts, tournaments/[id]/checkout|register/route.ts, credits/checkout/route.ts. Live: POST /api/duel/chips/match with no auth header returns 401, confirming withAuth still gates the handler ahead of assertPaidDuelAllowed, unaffected by this diff.

discoveryFindings.finding: With PAID_DUELS_ENABLED=false (server kill switch off) but NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED=true and an allowed region (CA), /duel's Chip Duels and Tournaments cards still show 'Not available in your region.' / 'unavailable' — the real reason is the kill switch, not geography. Reconfirmed live by me on a second local server instance (no rebuild needed, since PAID_DUELS_ENABLED is a server-only var read at process start). This is the reviewer's already-filed warning finding (destructuring only {allowed} and discarding {reason} from resolveRankedEligibility), not a regression introduced by this diff, and it is not a flash/first-paint defect — the (misleading) copy is consistent from the very first byte, and the free Quick Play / Challenge modes remain fully usable. Not a blocking AC failure.

The two combinations with NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED=false were validated by code inspection only, not live request, because that var is inlined into the built bundle at compile time and would have required a second full `pnpm build` for marginal additional confidence beyond what the reviewer already established for the boolean logic. Code inspection confirms both combinations render a clean hidden state on /duel with no broken/missing badge; /duel/chips remains reachable and functional if navigated to directly regardless of the client-side flag (pre-existing behavior, unrelated to this diff — ChipDuelLobby has always hardcoded enabled=true for its revalidation probe, per the reviewer's finding).

learnings.insight: For a Next.js App Router page, the embedded RSC/Flight payload serialized into the raw HTML response (searchable via grep for the prop name, e.g. 'initialGeoAllowed\":false') is direct proof of what value a server component resolved and handed to a client component — stronger evidence than the visible copy alone, and available in the exact same curl response used for the first-paint assertion. It rules out a 'the visible text happens to be right but the underlying serialized state is wrong and would flip on some client interaction' false pass.
learnings.action: When asserting first-paint correctness for a server-resolved prop passed into a client component, grep the raw HTML response for the prop's serialized name/value in the RSC payload, not just the rendered copy, for a stronger and cheaper signal than a render test.

learnings.insight: PAID_DUELS_ENABLED (server-only) and NEXT_PUBLIC_PAID_DUELS_ENABLED (client-inlined) behave completely differently under a local pnpm build/start cycle: the server var can be flipped by restarting `next start` with a different env var and no rebuild (it's read at process/module load time), but the NEXT_PUBLIC_ var is baked into the webpack bundle at `next build` time and restarting `next start` with a different value has zero effect. A QA pass that wants to exercise all four kill-switch combinations live needs either two separate `pnpm build`s (one per NEXT_PUBLIC_ value) or must fall back to code inspection for the combinations that differ only in the client-inlined var, and should say so explicitly rather than silently skipping them.
learnings.action: Before claiming to have 'tested all N env-var combinations locally,' identify which vars are NEXT_PUBLIC_ (build-time-inlined) vs server-only (runtime-read) and budget rebuilds accordingly, or explicitly downgrade the build-time-var combinations to code-inspection-only in the report.

learnings.insight: Backgrounding `pnpm start -p <port>` with a bare `&` in a Bash tool call is unreliable in this environment (one attempt returned exit code 144 with no server actually bound, another silently raced against a stale process still holding the port from an earlier `&` launch that `ps aux` did not clearly show as attributable). Using the tool's own `run_in_background: true` parameter and then polling the dedicated `.output` file was reliable and gave a clean EADDRINUSE error message when a port was already taken, which the manual `&` + nohup approach did not surface as clearly.
learnings.action: Prefer the Bash tool's `run_in_background` parameter over manual `&`/`nohup` for starting a long-lived local dev/prod server during QA; check `ps aux` for `next-server`/`next start` by name (not just the port) before declaring a port free, and kill by PID with `kill -9` if a normal stop doesn't clear a zombie holding the socket.
